title: Basic Greetings and Expressions
description: Nine short section lessons build the greetings one step at a time — Dumela, Dumelang, Le kae?, Ke teng, thank you, goodbye and the polite forms — with a review after every three sections and cultural tips at the end.

words.notes: The everyday greeting to one person.
The respectful title for a man. Add it to the greeting: Dumela Rra.
The respectful title for a woman — also the word for mother. Add it to the greeting: Dumela Mma.
Add Rra (Sir) when greeting a man respectfully.
Add Mma (Ma'am/Mrs) when greeting a woman respectfully.
Use this when you greet a group.
BoMma is the plural of Mma — the respectful way to address a group of women.
BoRra is the plural of Rra — the respectful way to address a group of men.
Le means 'and', so this greets a mixed group.

tips.heading: Cultural Context Tips
items: Respect is key, especially when speaking to elders. Use "Dumelang" and "Le kae?" with a calm tone and body language.
Use two hands when giving or receiving something as a sign of respect.
Avoid rushing greetings — small talk is part of the social glue in Setswana culture.
Titles matter when addressing elders or authority figures — add "Rra" (Sir) or "Mma" (Ma'am/Mrs).
Everyone greets when entering a room or meeting people.
Show respect to elders using "Rra" or "Mma" after greetings.
